content_of_post_to_comment:
I failed algebra in high school and never went to college until now (I’m 30). I’ve aced all my classes (25 credits so far) but have dropped out of algebra every time.

My first 3 attempts were online. This time I’m taking the course in person to stay on track. Historically, I get super anxious the first week and start my lessons a few days later than I should. I tend to procrastinate to avoid facing my fears. Next thing I know, I’m SUPER behind. When I would study for my online courses, I was able to grasp the concepts but the lessons took WAY too long for me to understand. I mean I would spend HOURS on a factoring out. By the time I got it, the lesson would toss in more complex information that took a few more hours to understand. I became exhausted knowing how much I had to learn to complete Module 0—yes 0. The first test typically covers modules 0-1/2.

Remembering all the new rules and vocabulary gets very overwhelming so I drop out when I realize I will never catch up.

The college requires I take a remedial course at the same time, but the online remedial course was basically useless. There were no lessons. I hope that learning in person is a different experience. The set up is that I’m taking two classes back to back. The first is remedial, the second is the credited course. If I can’t pass college algebra, I might as well drop out of school entirely and figure out a different path. Every degree path that I’m interested in requires this course + additional math courses. This is it for me.

My plan:
-Limited breaks are okay. Spending 8 hours on the computer for work and then studying for algebra back to back is exhausting to my eyes and brain. When I get home, I won’t immediately open my computer. I will run errands/do house work/eat. I will set a strict start time and end time for studying. Staying up too late, even for studying, results in bad sleep and ruins my brain the following day. Next thing I know my whole week is full of bad sleep and I spend the weekend playing catch up.

-If I’m not understanding a concept because of my professor’s teaching style or the awful Pearson lab videos, then I will not waste time trying to learn their teaching style. Instead, I will utilize the internet, YouTube, GetSchooled, KhanAcademy, etc. to learn. This was one of my biggest issues. Not everyone is great at teaching math and it’s up to me to find out who teaches at my learning level.

-USE CAMPUS RESOURCES FOR ASSISTANCE!!! I have never reached out to the tutoring lab. I need to take advantage of this free source which is located right next to my class.

Class starts tomorrow! This will be my first time in a classroom since 2014 😵‍💫.
